reason: The description is remarkably thorough and accurately captures nearly every helper function emitted by `writePreamble`: the debug helper, init_completion replacement, index_of_word, contains_word, handle_go_custom_completion (including directive parsing, alias-via-words[0], ActiveHelp disabling, empty-arg injection, all five directives), handle_reply (flag branch, flag-value-with-equals, flag_parsing_disabled fallthrough, prev-flag special handler, noun/command/alias completion, noun_aliases fallback, custom_func fallback, ltrim_colon_completions, single-flag nospace), handle_filename_extension_flag, handle_subdirs_in_dir_flag, handle_flag (flaghash, local_nonpersistent_flags clearing commands, two_word_flags skip, must_have_one_flag clearing), handle_noun (noun_aliases clearing must_have_one_noun), handle_command (last_command chaining, root_command at c==0), and handle_word (recursive traversal, alias resolution with aliashash, bash>3 guard). One minor omission is that handle_flag also clears `commands=()` when a local_nonpersistent_flag is seen, which the description does not mention. The description also does not explicitly mention that handle_word calls itself recursively at the end (tail recursion pattern). These are secondary details and do not materially impair implementability.
missing_functionality: handle_flag clears the `commands` array when the current flag is found in `local_nonpersistent_flags`; this side-effect is not mentioned.

handle_word calls itself recursively at the end of every branch (tail recursion), which is the mechanism that advances through all words; the description says 'recursively walk' but attributes the recursion to handle_command rather than handle_word itself.
handle_command resolves the next function name by replacing colons with double-underscores (`words[c]//:/__`); this naming convention is not described.
incorrect_or_misleading_points: The description says the debug helper uses 'an environment variable' without naming it; the implementation uses `BASH_COMP_DEBUG_FILE`, which is a concrete detail but not strictly wrong.
The description attributes alias resolution to handle_command, but in the implementation alias lookup (aliashash) happens in handle_word before delegating to handle_command.
